clue.text: Ward Osborne off — he can go downhill fast

indicators.note: off in the sense of gone bad or wrong, so the letters of the two names are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone called Ward Osborne is unwell, or leaving, while the clue muses about a person speeding downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: The name reads like a politician (George Osborne was Chancellor), but it is simply eleven letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider on a single board slides down snowy slopes at speed, so this is a description of the sportsman.

clue.text: Prisoner at the back of emergency transporter

parts.note: a lifer is a prisoner serving a life sentence
aft is the nautical word for at or towards the rear of a ship

explanation.surface: A prisoner rides in the rear of an emergency vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflatable boat carried for shipwrecks transports survivors in an emergency, a cryptic description.

clue.text: Blast! Flipping Miliband gave me the eye!

indicators.note: flipping turns the exclamation over, so its letters are read from the end back to the start

parts.note: Rats! and Blast! are both exclamations of annoyance
Ed Miliband was leader of the Labour Party

explanation.surface: Someone curses as the Labour leader shoots them a look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British swear word to go with 'Blast!', but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone the eye is to look hard at them, which is a fixed gaze.

clue.text: Lib Dem leader's broadcast an irritant for Derby candidates

definitions.meaning: the Liberal Democrat leader Nick Clegg's name, said aloud, sounds like cleg, a dialect word for a biting fly of horses and cattle
racehorses entered for the Derby are pestered by this biting insect

explanation.surface: A party political broadcast by the Liberal Democrat leader irritates voters like a pest.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is Britain's most famous flat horse race. Cleg (sounding like Clegg) is a regional name for the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The biting gadfly torments horses, so it is a nuisance to any racehorse.

clue.text: Enjoy this dance rhythm

definitions.meaning: in slang to ... on something is to enjoy it
a strong regular beat that makes music good to dance to

explanation.surface: An invitation to enjoy this dance beat.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang verb for liking something; also the swinging beat in a piece of dance music.

clue.text: Policies? Environment and sustainability primarily for Greens

indicators.note: primarily, meaning first of all, picks out the opening letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: The Green Party's policies centre on the environment and sustainability.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greens' looks like the political party, but it means green vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Peas are green vegetables, and greens is a general word for such vegetables; peas are one example.

clue.text: Tension generated by topless frolics outside Number 10

indicators.note: outside says the shortened merriment sits around the other letters
topless means without its top, so the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: gaiety is merrymaking, frolics
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Political strain arises from naked high jinks outside the Prime Minister's residence.
explanation.walkthrough: Number 10 Downing Street is the British Prime Minister's home; here it splits into N and X, which go inside AIETY.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervous worry is a state of mental strain, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: See 1
Pretty short message

indicators.note: short means cut short, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a tweet is a short message posted on Twitter

explanation.surface: A quite brief message, or a pretty little note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty' looks like an adverb meaning quite, qualifying 'short'; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee describes something quaintly or excessively pretty and dainty.

clue.text: UKIP not suitable for everyone, suspends transatlantic services

parts.note: U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for everyone; take it from UKIP to leave KIP, a nap, which means rest
to suspend something is to stop it

explanation.surface: A jibe that UKIP is not for all voters and is halting services to America.
explanation.walkthrough: U-certificate films are suitable for all ages; dropping the U from UKIP leaves KIP, British slang for a sleep, so a rest.
explanation.definitionFit: American English for roadside service areas, so services described in transatlantic terms.

clue.text: Dacre's tricked Galloway, perhaps — it's above criticism

indicators.note: tricked as in tricked out or fooled, so the newspaper editor's name is jumbled

parts.note: Galloway is a Scottish breed of cattle, so an example of a cow

explanation.surface: Daily Mail editor Paul Dacre has duped the politician George Galloway.
explanation.walkthrough: Galloway looks like the outspoken MP, but it is the cattle breed; 'perhaps' marks an example. 'tricked' rearranges DACRES to SACRED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held sacrosanct is an idea or institution that nobody is allowed to criticise, an idiom.

clue.text: Tartan cloth for the party

definitions.meaning: a chequered woollen fabric in a clan pattern
... Cymru is the Welsh nationalist party, often called simply ...

explanation.surface: Choosing tartan material for a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Checked twill fabric; also the short name of Wales's nationalist political party.

clue.text: Before or after electoral method number one?

indicators.note: after places the word or behind the other pieces

parts.note: PR is proportional representation, a voting system
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A question whether something comes before or after the main voting system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is not a link here but the letters themselves, placed after PR and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier in time or order; prior to means before, a synonym.

clue.text: Eaterie with a continental stimulant

parts.note: a caff is British slang for a cheap cafe
eine is German for a, so a word for a on the Continent

explanation.surface: A cafe offers a European pick-me-up.
explanation.walkthrough: A caff is an informal British cafe serving fried breakfasts and tea.
explanation.definitionFit: The alkaloid in coffee and tea that perks the drinker up is a mild stimulant drug.

clue.text: Mineral turning up in travertine

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means read upwards, so the letters run backwards
in says the letters are found inside the word travertine

explanation.surface: A mineral appears in a kind of limestone.
explanation.definitionFit: Potassium nitrate occurs naturally as a crystalline mineral, saltpetre.

clue.text: It's spotted before penultimate vote in Parliament

indicators.note: before puts the spotted cube ahead of the chosen letter

parts.note: a die (one of a pair of dice) is spotted with dots

indicators.note: penultimate means last but one, so take the second-from-last letter of vote

explanation.surface: Something is noticed ahead of the second-last vote in the Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted' seems to mean seen; it means marked with spots, like a die.
explanation.definitionFit: A diet is the legislative assembly of certain countries, such as Japan's national assembly.

clue.text: American author's Fourth of July verse

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer; with the possessive this gives his name plus S

indicators.note: Fourth of picks the fourth letter of the month name

explanation.surface: A US writer's poem for Independence Day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fourth of July' looks like the American holiday, but it gives only the letter Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Poesy is an old word for poetry, so it is a synonym of verse.

clue.text: Papers vote for the Left

parts.note: a house that votes for a bill passes it
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Newspapers urge readers to back the left-wing party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Papers' looks like the press; it means travel documents. 'the Left' is the side of a ship, not the political wing.
explanation.definitionFit: Travellers carry identity papers; the official travel document is one such paper.

clue.text: Slugs for children

definitions.meaning: a slug is a swig or shot of spirits, a small measure of drink

explanation.surface: Garden pests suitable for youngsters.
explanation.definitionFit: Small measures of whisky; also informal for toddlers.

clue.text: Cable to phone Mrs Simpson back

parts.note: tel is the abbreviation for telephone

indicators.note: back means the name is turned round and read from the end

parts.note: Marge Simpson is the mother in the cartoon The Simpsons

explanation.surface: A wire to ring Mrs Simpson in return.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Simpson suggests Wallis Simpson, of the abdication, but it is Marge from the cartoon.
explanation.definitionFit: A cable was an overseas wired message, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Is racist organisation dividing Farage constituents?

definitions.note: AGE is a run of letters inside Farage; a geological period is a division of time, splitting an age or era

indicators.note: organisation is the act of arranging, so the letters of the two words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A question asking whether a racist group is splitting Nigel Farage's voters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituents' looks like voters in Farage's seat; it means the letters that make up his name, which hold AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: The early Mesozoic period is a division of geological time, a span within a larger age.

clue.text: Tree-hugger repeatedly getting Sturgeon's vote?

indicators.note: repeatedly says the vote is given twice over

parts.note: aye is a yes vote, and Scots like Nicola Sturgeon say aye for yes

explanation.surface: An environmentalist keeps winning the SNP leader's support.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicola Sturgeon led the Scottish National Party. 'Tree-hugger' looks like an environmentalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A Madagascan lemur that lives in trees, clinging to branches, so literally a tree-hugger.

clue.text: Labour leader in a hole — produce new poll?

indicators.note: in says the leading letter sits inside the hollow

parts.note: a cave is a hole in rock

indicators.note: leader means the front letter of Labour

explanation.surface: The Labour leader is in trouble and wonders about calling a fresh election.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poll' looks like a vote, but a poll is also a hornless cow or bullock.
explanation.definitionFit: To give birth to a young cow is to produce a new animal of the hornless kind.

clue.text: Fat lady singing here? Rattled Cameron gives nothing away

indicators.note: rattled means shaken up, so the remaining letters are jumbled
gives with away says a letter is surrendered from the name
away completes gives away, saying a letter leaves the name

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A shaken David Cameron gives nothing away; is it all over, as the saying about the fat lady goes?
explanation.walkthrough: 'It ain't over till the fat lady sings' refers to opera, where large sopranos sing. Dropping O from CAMERON leaves CAMERN, which 'Rattled' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Bizet's opera is a place where a soprano might sing, the fat lady of the saying.

clue.text: Stage a coup? Balls might

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls
might is strength, power

explanation.surface: Whether to seize power, with a crude retort that guts might do it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might' looks like a verb; it is a noun meaning strength. An over in cricket is six deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebels who mount a coup subdue the government by force, which is to subdue or conquer it.

clue.text: Fine wine? No time!

indicators.note: No says the letter for time is absent from the wine

parts.note: Tokay is a sweet Hungarian wine

explanation.surface: Someone asks if the wine is good and is told there is no time.
explanation.definitionFit: All right, acceptable: an informal synonym meaning satisfactory.

clue.text: Jeer and grunt before beginning and end

parts.note: grunt is US slang for an infantry soldier, a GI

indicators.note: beginning and end picks the first and last letters of the word before

explanation.surface: Mocking and grunting from start to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grunt' seems a noise, but it is a soldier; 'before' is not a position word but the source of the letters B and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A taunt or mocking remark is a jeer; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: B — O = b

parts.note: on a family tree b. abbreviates the word for coming into the world, so the bare letter b equals that word

explanation.walkthrough: Genealogies write b. for the date of birth; the clue's formula reads B, then O, equals b, the letter string starting with B and O.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation b in genealogy and biographies stands for the past participle of bear, came into being.

clue.text: Tackle man with three feet

parts.note: Hal is a man's name, short for Henry
a yard is three feet

explanation.surface: A rugby player tackles a man with three legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tackle' looks like a verb; it is a noun meaning ship's rigging.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope for hoisting a sail or flag is part of a ship's rigging, its gear or tackle.

clue.text: Withdraws research about two ducks

indicators.note: about says the abbreviation goes round the cricketing failure

parts.note: res is an abbreviation for research
in cricket a pair is two ducks, out for no runs in both innings

explanation.surface: A scientist retracts a study of a couple of waterfowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ducks' looks like birds; in cricket a duck is a score of nought.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair to a place is an old formal way of saying to go or retire there, so withdraws.
